name: CrewAI
tagline: Teams of AI agents with defined roles and tasks
description: Python framework for orchestrating teams of AI agents with explicit roles and tasks, minimal boilerplate and integration with several models.
priceNote: Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Prototyping and running agent teams with a well-defined role
pros: Simple mental model of agent, task and expected output, which the business side understands
A few lines of code to assemble a complete team with roles and tools
Works with models from several providers, so you can swap models without rewriting the crew
Supports sequential or hierarchical execution, which suits more complex flows
cons: Depends on an external language model, and cost per token is the largest share of the bill
Poorly scoped agents burn tokens repeating work until they hit the iteration limit
Documentation changed a lot in recent releases and many public examples are out of date
No ready-made observability like LangSmith, and without logs debugging an agent is hard

features.name: Agents with a role
features.detail: Each agent has its own goal, context and tool list

features.name: Chained tasks
features.detail: You define the work sequence and the expected format of each deliverable

features.name: Flexible processes
features.detail: Sequential or hierarchical execution, with context passed between agents

features.name: Tools and MCP
features.detail: Connects APIs, web search and internal systems through ready-made tools

features.name: Cloud deployment
features.detail: Managed platform with scheduled runs, logs and observability

useCases: Research crew that cross-checks the sales report, customer feedback and market data before the meeting
Agent team that drafts the campaign, generates ad variations and reviews the final copy
Research routine that produces a biweekly industry report with sources and an executive summary
Agents that fill in a commercial proposal by querying the catalog and current margins
bestForWho: Engineering or data teams that want to prototype a multi-agent system fast and then evolve to production.
verdict: CrewAI is still the shortest path from zero to a running team of agents, because the concept of an agent with a role and a task is immediate even for people who do not code. What misleads people is assuming the ready-made crew is the product: in practice the work lies in defining the task, the output format and the iteration limit, and without those the agent team loops and burns tokens. The other point is the absence of native observability, which forces you to plug in LangSmith or your own tracing. For a small company, use the local library for specific tasks and pay only for what you consume. For a larger company, the paid cloud platform earns its keep through run history and access roles, but require readable logs before you scale.
